claims.claim: Revision 3 title: Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management: A CSF 2.0 Community Profile

Revision 2 depicted a circular life cycle; incidents were relatively rare and recovery usually completed within a day or two; today recovery often takes weeks or months and lessons should be shared as soon as identified
Govern, Identify and Protect preparation activities are not part of the incident response itself; incident response is Detect, Respond and Recover; Improvement (ID.IM) is the middle level
claims.locator: Section 2.1, text under Fig. 2: 'The bottom level reflects that the preparation activities of Govern, Identify, and Protect are not part of the incident response itself'

Definition of a cybersecurity incident used by Revision 3

quiz_map.support: The document is explicit that the preparation activities of Govern, Identify and Protect are not part of the incident response itself.
Pick the category of the earliest step for containment and list the others for scoping.
Write the AI equivalents down: who may revoke a production key, disable a connector or pause an agent at three in the morning.
Assess each applicable impact dimension, give it a score from 1 to 4, and take the **highest** score as the overall severity.
`UpdateAgentActionGroup` carries `actionGroupState`, whose valid values are `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`; it specifies whether the action group is available for the agent to invoke.
Microsoft states that non-deterministic behaviour cannot be verified through a single test pass, and asks for watch periods with explicit closure criteria after each stage.
The SOC's job is to know the clocks exist and to supply facts quickly.
Before changing anything, the analyst exports the two conversations with their retrieved context and records the document's identifier and upload details.
Writing this inventory is Identify work, and deciding who may pull each kill switch is Govern work.
The overall severity is the highest score in any single dimension, not the average.
Each category has one first move: revoke the key, disable the tool, disable the connector, restrict the access, quarantine the source.
userIdentity.arn names the role and the session, for example an assumed role called soc-responder with the session name of the analyst.
Inactive means the key cannot be used for programmatic calls, and the change can be reversed by setting the status back to Active.
Search CloudTrail for bedrock.amazonaws.com events signed with the contained key after the change.
requestParameters.accessKeyId is the key that was changed.
A contained key, tool or connector is switched back on only with the incident lead's approval recorded in the incident ticket, after eradication is complete.
Preserve comes before contain, and verify comes straight after it.
When that rule fires on the responders' own recorded action, the verdict is benign true positive: the rule worked and the activity was authorised.
Whether a duty applies is decided by legal, not by the SOC.
One clean test proves little, because the same input can produce a different output next time.
What an exercise reveals is treated like a lesson from a real incident: it goes to Improvement and changes the playbook the same week.
